title: Diseconomies of Scale
page_title: Diseconomies of Scale | Edexcel IGCSE Business Revision Notes 2017

blocks.name: Diseconomies of scale
blocks.definition:
Diseconomies of scale: 
• limits of growth.

blocks.md:
- As a firm continues increasing its **scale of output**, it will reach a point where its **average costs (AC)** will start to **increase**

  - The reasons for the increase in the average costs are called ***diseconomies of scale***

blocks.text: Diseconomies of scale and average costs

blocks.alt: Graph of long-run average costs showing a U-shape; economies of scale decrease costs, diseconomies increase costs, with lowest cost at efficient output.
blocks.caption: Diseconomies of scale occur when average costs increase with increasing output

blocks.md:
- At some level of output, a firm will **not be able to reduce costs** any further. This point is called **productive efficiency**
- Beyond this level of output, the average cost will begin to rise as a result of **diseconomies of scale**
- This indicates that there is an optimal level of output that exists when the state of technology and capital (machinery) is fixed

- Diseconomies of scale highlight that it is possible for a business to become so **large that it becomes less and less efficient**
- A business experiencing diseconomies of scale may **reconsider its organisational structure** to improve communication and coordination problems

  - Many very large businesses often **break themselves up into *****autonomous*** **smaller units, **which can communicate more effectively

| **Type** | **Explanation** | |---|---| | **Poor communication and coordination** | - As a business increases in size, **more managers and employees will join the business** and the ***chain of command*** is likely to lengthen, limiting** interaction with employees**
- **Communication** **becomes slower** and mistakes may be made, leading to** worsening efficiency**
- **Time-consuming decision-making **may make it harder to coordinate workers and physical resources | | **Increased bureaucracy** | - Larger businesses are more **complicated to run and organise** than small businesses
- Coordinating the **many resources required** will require extensive **administration **for which staff and physical resources will be required | | **Lack of commitment from employees** | - As the business grows **workers may feel less valued** as their interaction with management is limited
- Workers may **become demotivated** leading to a fall in output which can increase average costs |

blocks.label: Exam Hint
blocks.md: Candidates frequently confuse economies and diseconomies of scale in exams. Make sure that you can define both terms and give examples of why each could arise.
